samples.summary: Unblocked spill anchors are added to the recalculation set *after* `buildDependantsMap`, so cells that depend on the recovered anchor keep stale values
Drag-moving a range that contains a spill leaves ghost cells behind at the source and duplicates them at the destination with a stale `spillAnchor`
samples.evidence: `movedGrid` is built from `fetchGrid(normalizedSource)`, which returns every stored cell in the range including spill ghosts (`{ v, spillAnchor: <oldAnchorSref> }`); those objects are copied verbatim to the destination (`movedGrid.set(newSref, { ...cell })`, line 2348) so the destination gets ghost cells pointing at an anchor sref that no longer holds that spill. At the same time the source-clear loop does `if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;` (line 2389), so the original ghosts are *not* deleted from the source. Result: ghost values are visible in two places, and the copies at the destination can never be cleaned up by the calculator (its cleanup only deletes cells whose `spillAnchor === sref` at `anchorRef + offset`). This is in the function this diff modifies and interacts directly with the new spill-blocker bookkeeping (the new `consumeSpillBlocker` calls are skipped for exactly those `continue`d cells); it appears pre-existing rather than introduced here.

samples.summary: `setData`'s blocked-anchor handling unconditionally overwrites the anchor's dependants set, dropping real dependants — inconsistent with the guarded form the diff adopts
samples.evidence: `dependantsMap.set(blockedAnchor, new Set())` at line 1116 has no `if (!dependantsMap.has(...))` guard, unlike the new code in `moveRangeTo` (line 2479) and `removeData` (line 1196). If the blocked anchor already had dependants discovered by `buildDependantsMap`, they are erased and never recalculated. The diff establishes the guarded form as the intended contract, making this divergence a latent bug on the sibling path.

samples.summary: `refusalMessage` uses `default:` for the autofill case, so any future `RangeOpRefusal` value silently shows the wrong message with no compile-time check
`cleanup()` leaves the refusal callback registered on the Sheet, so a notice can fire (and a toast appear) after the view is torn down
samples.evidence: `initialize` registers `this.sheet.setOnRefusal((refusal) => this.onNoticeCallback?.(refusalMessage(refusal)))`. `cleanup()` sets `this.sheet = undefined` (line 588) but never clears `onNoticeCallback` nor unregisters the callback from the Sheet. The drag-move/autofill completion handlers run inside `void (async () => ...)()` and explicitly tolerate teardown mid-flight (`if (!this.sheet) return;`), so a refusal resolved after unmount still invokes the host toast callback, and the Sheet keeps a strong reference to the destroyed Worksheet.

samples.summary: Other silent no-op exits of the same gestures still give no notice, so the stated goal ("never look like the drag did nothing") is only partly met
samples.evidence: `moveRangeTo` returns silently at line 2296 (`if (this.pivotDefinition) return;`), and `autofill` returns silently at `selectionType !== 'cell'` (line 2559) — both are user-initiated gestures reachable from the drag handlers in `view/worksheet.ts` (4340, 4195) that produce exactly the silent no-op this change exists to eliminate. Only the three merge-related refusals report. Not a regression, but the guard set is incomplete.

finding.summary: Unblocked spill anchors are added to the recalculation set *after* `buildDependantsMap`, so cells that depend on the recovered anchor keep stale values

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism does not exist in this repository. It assumes `store.buildDependantsMap(seed)` produces a map limited to edges reachable from the seed, so that inserting unblocked anchors afterwards leaves the anchor with no outgoing edges. Every Store implementation here ignores the seed and returns a full-grid map: YorkieStore does `void srefs;` and scans all formula cells (yorkie-store.ts:560-612), MemStore's parameter is `_` and it iterates the whole grid (memory.ts:319-342), ReadOnlyStore returns an empty map unconditionally (readonly.ts:147-151); the `IDBStore` mentioned in the memory.ts comment does not exist in the tree. Hence `buildDependantsMap(expanded)` already contains `anchor -> {cells referencing anchor}`, and `buildDependantsMap(new Set([...expanded, ...unblockedAnchors]))` would return the identical map. Additionally, the `dependantsMap.set(anchor, new Set())` line is gated by `if (!dependantsMap.has(anchor))`, so it can never overwrite existing dependant edges; and when it does fire it is a no-op because `topologicalSort` pushes the ref and only recurses `if (dependantsMap.has(ref))` (calculator.ts:189-198), so an absent key and an empty set behave identically. Seeding the anchor into `expanded` is sufficient: DFS from the seed walks out through the complete map and `calculate` re-evaluates dependants after the anchor (calculator.ts:46-47), so a formula like `=A4*2` is refreshed once the spill recovers.

finding.evidence: `movedGrid` is built from `fetchGrid(normalizedSource)`, which returns every stored cell in the range including spill ghosts (`{ v, spillAnchor: <oldAnchorSref> }`); those objects are copied verbatim to the destination (`movedGrid.set(newSref, { ...cell })`, line 2348) so the destination gets ghost cells pointing at an anchor sref that no longer holds that spill. verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described and reachable. `fetchGrid` -> `MemoryStore.getGrid` (memory.ts:145-157) returns all stored cells including spill ghosts, and sheet.ts:2348 copies them verbatim (`{ ...cell }`) to the destination with a stale `spillAnchor`. The source-clear loop at sheet.ts:2389 `continue`s on `sourceCell?.spillAnchor`, so source ghosts are never deleted (and consumeSpillBlocker at 2392 is skipped for them). No later cleanup reaps either copy: `calculate` skips formula-less cells (calculator.ts:49-51) so the deleted source anchor never runs its ghost cleanup, and that cleanup only deletes cells at the (new) anchorRef+offset whose spillAnchor equals that anchor's sref (calculator.ts:74-85). The orphans are also user-unremovable (setData early-returns at sheet.ts:1072; removeData skips at sheet.ts:1150). No guard upstream: the sole production caller worksheet.ts:4340 only checks for a same-origin drop, and moveRangeTo's only refusals are merge-related (sheet.ts:2326-2337). Result is duplicated/ghost data and a broken spill invariant — a real major correctness defect.
